 : Judgment :
This petition has been referred by the Addl. Land Acquisition Officer, B.D.A., Bengaluru for enhancement of compensation in respect of land acquired.

.2. The specific claim of the claimants in this case is that the claimants are the owners of the property bearing Sy. No. 50/2 measuring 29 guntas of Devarachikkanahalli village, Beguru Hobli,
Bangaluru South Taluka and the said property has been acquired for the purpose of BTM IV stage.

-3- : L.A.C. No.20/2008 :
Preliminary Notification issued on 06.08.1988 under Section 17 of the B.D.A. Act and the same has been published on 29.12.1988 and thereafter, Final Notification under Section 19 of the B.D.A. Act issued on 03.11.1990 and the same has been published on 20.11.1990.

It is also made out by the claimants that the LAO registered a case in L.A.C. No. 92/1990-91 and the General Award has been passed, wherein, awarded compensation of Rs. 90,000/- per acre in respect of dry land, Rs.
1,10,000/- in respect of wet and garden land and Rs. 60,000/- in respect of phoot kharab land.

It is further stated that the claimant No.12 being a GPA holder of claimants 1 to 11 filed an application before the LAO under Section 18 (3)(b) of the Land Acquisition Act for enhancement of compensation, but they have not referred the said application to the Court.

Hence, filed a petition before this Court under Section 18(3)(b) of the Land Acquisition Act, that has been numbered as L.A.C. No. 208/2000 on the file of this Court and as per the order passed in L.A.C. No.208/2000,
the Court allowed the petition and issued direction to the respondent to make a reference to the Court.

The said order has been challenged before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka by the respondent in CRP No. 1945/2003, that came to be dismissed as on 30.11.2005 and confirmed the order made by the reference Court under Section 18(3)(b) of the Land Acquisition Act as on 11.04.2003.
Further it is stated that the LAO has made the reference under Sections 30 and 31 of Land Acquisition Act in L.A.C. No.23/1996 and the same was disposed off.
Accordingly prayed to enhance the compensation @ Rs. 200/- per Sq. feet in respect of acquired property of the claimants.

.3. On the basis of the said direction, the LAO made the reference to the Court and after receipt of this case, the notice has been issued to the parties and the parties have appeared before the Court.

On the basis of the above, the points for consideration are as that:
1) Whether the claim petition is barred by limitation under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act?
2) Whether the compensation awarded by the opponent / respondent is inadequate?

If so, what compensation claimants are entitled?
3) What order or award?
.6. In support of their case, the GPA holder of the claimants 1 to 11 examined himself as PW.1 by filing evidence affidavit and also got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10.

The respondent filed I.A. No.1/22 under Section 151 of CPC praying to discard the evidence of PW.1 claiming that the claimants 1 to 11 were not properly authorized the GPA holder to prosecute the case.

Accordingly the GPA holder was directed to keep the claimants 1 to 11 present before the Court and even the learned counsel representing for claimants as on 06.07.2022 submitted that the GPA holder remained absent and parties are not ready to appear before the Court.
Considering all these facts, the evidence of PW.1 has been discarded.

Subsequently the case was posted for -6- : L.A.C. No.20/2008 :
evidence, but they have failed to lead further evidence.
In view of the order passed by the Court in L.A.C. No. 208/2000, the case has been referred to this Court.
Hence this Court taken up for disposal on merits.
The Sheristedar in the office of respondent has been examined as RW.1.
Thereafter the evidence of RW.1 has been discarded on 26.07.2017 in view of the memo filed by the advocate for respondent.
Thereafter, the Superintendent in the office of respondent has been examined as RW.2.

The documents marked at Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2.
.7.
The claimants failed to appear before the Court to advance the arguments.

Heard the arguments of the respondent and perused the material on record, on that basis my findings on the above point No. 1 in the affirmative, point No.2 in the negative and point No.3 as per final order, for the following:
REASONS .8. POINT NO.1:

The claimants have approached the Court with allegation that the respondent / ALAO has -7- : L.A.C. No.20/2008 :

Hence, the claimants filed the petition before the Court under Section 18(3)(b) of the Land Acquisition Act, that has been numbered as L.A.C. No.208/2000 and in the said case,
the Court allowed the petition and directed the respondent to make a reference to the Court.
Accordingly, the reference has been made to the Court.

.9. In this case, the respondent has taken up a specific contention in the objection that this petition is hopelessly barred by limitation and there is an inordinate delay in filing the application for enhancement hence the Court is bound to consider the fact that whether this reference is well within prescribed limitation period as contemplated under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act.
Under such circumstances, it -8- : L.A.C. No.20/2008 :

is for the claimants to show that they have filed application for enhancement of compensation praying the Land Acquisition Officer to make the reference to the Court to determine the proper market value within the period of limitation under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act.
.10.

It is undisputed fact in this case that the Preliminary Notification under Section 17 of the B.D.A. Act has been issued as on 06.08.1988 and the same has been published on 29.12.1988 and Final Notification under Section 19 of the B.D.A. Act has been issued as on 03.11.1990 and the same has been published as on 20.11.1990.
Therefore, the notifications for acquisition have been published in the year 1990.
Apart from that, the LAO has registered the case in L.A.C. No.92/1990-91 to determine the market value of the acquired property and he has passed the General Award.

It is surprising to note that the claimants nowhere stated that when actually General Award in L.A.C. No. 92/90-91 was passed and why the said fact has been suppressed by the claimants is not at all explained.

At this juncture, it is -9- : L.A.C. No.20/2008 :
relevant to note that the claimants stated in para No. 8 of the claim statement that:
"It is further submitted that the LAO made a reference under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act in L.A.C. No. 23/1996 and the same was disposed off."
If this averment in the claim statement is accepted, it has to be accepted that these claimants/ petitioners were aware of the passing of award by the LAO.

Hence, the Munireddy C V vs Addl Lao on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51623099/
4 claimants must show that when they came to know about the passing of award by the LAO or they were totally unaware of the proceedings in L.A.C. No. 23/1996.

sentences.text:
If at all these claimants have appeared in L.A.C. No. 23/1996, then it has to be inferred that they have the knowledge of the General Award passed by the LAO.
.11.

It is relevant to note that the claimants have produced the order passed in L.A.C.
No. 23/1996 as per Ex.P.9.
As per the said document, this Court disposed off the said case in L.A.C. No. 23/1996 as on 02.07.2003.

As per the said document, all the claimants appeared through their advocate Sri. P. Krishnappa and in the said case,
the Court has allowed the reference and held that the claimants are - 10 : L.A.C. No.20/2008 :
entitled for compensation in respect of Sy. No. 50/2 measuring 29 guntas of land.
Therefore, it is clear that these applicants have raised objections for grant of compensation before the LAO.
As such, the LAO has made the reference to the Court under Sections 30 and 31 of Land Acquisition Act.
Accordingly the reference has been registered before this Court in L.A.C. No. 23/1996.
Therefore, undisputedly the reference under Sections 30 and 31 of Land Acquisition Act has been registered in respect of the property involved in this case in the year 1996.
Hence, it has to be inferred that the claimants have the knowledge of award passed by the LAO at- least in the year 1996.
Hence, considering this fact, the Court has to consider whether the petition is within time as contemplated under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act.

Before proceeding further in this case, it is just and necessary to note the said provision under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, that reads as under:
"18. Reference to Court (1)Any person interested who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector, require that - 11 : L.A.C. No.20/2008 :
the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Court, whether his objection be to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the persons to whom it is payable, or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested.
(2)The application shall state the grounds on which objection to the award is taken:Provided that every such application shall be made,
(a)if the person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when he made his award, within six weeks from the date of the Collectors award;
(b)in other cases, within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under section 12, sub-section (2), or within six months from the date of the Collectors Munireddy C V vs Addl Lao on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51623099/
5 award, whichever period shall first expire."
Therefore, as per Section 18(2)(a) & (b), the claimants ought to have filed an application for enhancement of compensation requesting to make the reference to the Court within 6 weeks from the date of Collectors award or within 6 weeks from the date of service of award notice under Section 12(2) of the Land Acquisition Act.

Of-course it is a provision of Central Acts and the same has been amended by Karnataka Acts and as per the Karnataka Amended Acts, 90 - 12 : L.A.C. No.20/2008 :
days time has been granted to make an application for reference under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act or to make the reference to the Court for enhancement of compensation.

Therefore, even if the knowledge of claimants regarding passing of the award as on 31.12.1996, then also the claimants ought to have filed an application before the LAO on or before 31.03.1997.
.12.
Now it is to be considered the certified copy of the acknowledgment and copy of application filed before the LAO for enhancement of compensation at Ex.P.3 and 2 respectively.
As per Ex.P.3 certified copy of acknowledgment, the acknowledgment has been issued as on 14.02.2000.
However, the seal found in Ex.P.2 at the top of first page shows that the application submitted to the LAO as on 06.06.2000.
Therefore, the GPA holder of the claimants 1 to 11 filed an application under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act before the LAO in the year 2000 i.e., almost after a lapse of 3 years.
Therefore, viewed from any angle the very application filed by the GPA holder of the claimants 1 to 11 is barred by limitation.

.13 . In the case on hand, the respondent seriously disputed the status of claimant No.12 as GPA holder and the respondent totally disputed the execution of any GPA by claimants 1 to 11 in his favour.
When such is the case, it is for the GPA holder to keep all the claimants present before the Court and to show that they have executed the GPA in his favour to prosecute the case.
Further no application has been filed by the claimants before the LAO for enhancement.

Therefore, even if there is any GPA executed by the claimants 1 to 11 in favour of claimant No. 12,
then also he has to file an application within the time prescribed under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act.
As this application hopelessly barred by limitation, certainly the claimants have not entitled for enhancement of any compensation as claimed in the petition.

Of course, there is a direction by the Court to make a reference, that itself is not a ground to accept the case of the claimants for enhancement as claimants failed to make out any case to show that petition is well within time and they are totally unaware of the proceedings in L.A.C. No. 23/1996.

No. 23/1996 is the General Power of Attorney Holder of claimants 1 to 11, then also it has to consider that when the General Power of Attorney holder has the knowledge of land acquisition proceedings and the case.

Even according to Ex.P.7-General Power of Attorney produced in this case shows that original claimants have executed the General Power of Attorney as on 20.08.1992 but that has not been got marked by the P.W.1.
However copy of the said GPA is found in the file.

Under such circumstances,
it has to be accepted that the claimant No. 12 has the knowledge of the award passed by the LAO and proceedings in L.A.C. No. 23/1996.

Further It is relevant to note that the execution of the General Power of Attorney as on 20.08.1992 is subsequent to the Preliminary Notification and Final Notification and condition No.4 in the said General Power of Attorney dated 20.08.1992 reads as:
" To file necessary application, objection statement or any other application before the Land Acquisition Officer of Government, Bengaluru Development Authority,
Corporation of the City of Bengaluru for the purpose of claiming the - 15 : L.A.C. No.20/2008 :
 compensation or for praying for  enhancement of compensation."

Therefore, this condition also sufficiently shows that this GPA holder has the knowledge of land acquisition as well as passing of the award by the LAO and also reference made by the LAO to the Court under Sections 30 and 31 of Land Acquisition Act, which was numbered in L.A.C. No. 23/1996.
Hence, this reference or application filed by the claimants before the LAO as per Ex.P.2 in the year 2000 is certainly barred by limitation.
Accordingly, the point No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
.15. Point No.2:
In view of my finding on point No.1, the question of determining the market value does not arise at all.
Accordingly, the above point No.2 is answered in the negative.
.16. Point No.3:

In views of my findings on the above points 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The reference/petition filed by the claimants under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 is hereby dismissed.
The order passed by the LAO is hereby  confirmed.
No order as to cost.
